answer: Size each identity's bond to the reward it can actually touch, not a flat fee. A low-stakes seat posts a saffron-small deposit; one reaching for large payouts must lock proportionally more, so a farmer cannot ripple one cheap bond across a thousand high-value clones. Fraud forfeits the walnut-hard deposit, and because the lock always exceeds what that seat could steal, every fake is net-negative by construction.
